events.text: Sichuan hot pot, so spicy that grown martial artists weep into it. The cook dares you to try the red side.

ok.log: You finish the bowl. The cook bows. The whole restaurant applauds.

fail.log: You set yourself on fire from the inside. The cook brings you milk and a lecture.

effects.log: 'Coward,' says the cook, with love.

events.text: Your neighbours in Sichuan are polite, quiet and very careful never to accept food from strangers. They are distant Tang cousins.

effects.log: They thank you, and quietly test the cakes with a silver needle before eating them.
They smile, change the subject, and your door has an extra lock the next morning. From the inside.

events.text: Nuns from Mount Emei come down to the market to buy salt. The bandits in the market suddenly remember appointments elsewhere.

effects.log: The eldest nun asks your name, and remembers it. That is unusual for Emei.
You have never seen men walk that fast without running.

events.text: The plank road clings to the cliff over a gorge. The planks are older than your grandparents and just as creaky.

ok.log: You run the planks like a monkey. A merchant stops to applaud.

fail.log: A plank breaks. You hang by one hand for a very long moment.

choices.text: Cross it slowly, eyes on the next plank

effects.log: It takes an hour. You arrive with every limb.

events.text: In the bamboo forest you meet a black-and-white bear eating bamboo with total concentration. It does not care about you at all.

effects.log: It eats for three hours. You learn more about focus than from any master.
It takes the bamboo, looks at you with deep indifference, and continues.

events.text: The Sichuan mountains are wrapped in mist so thick you cannot see your own feet. Somewhere ahead, a bell rings.

effects.log: A hermitage, a monk and a cup of tea. You never find it again.

choices.text: Wait for the mist to lift

effects.log: It lifts at noon. The view makes you forget where you were going.

events.text: The salt wells of Sichuan go down a thousand feet. The workers who haul the brine are stronger than most sect disciples.

choices.text: Work the wells for a season

effects.log: Your shoulders double in size. (20 taels)
He wins. He buys you a meal for trying.

events.text: A signpost on a mountain road reads, in three hands: 'Ten Thousand Poison Valley. Turn back. We mean it. Really.'

effects.log: Wise. You hear later that a whole bandit gang ignored the sign.

ok.log: You find a patch of rare herbs at the valley edge and leave very quickly.

fail.log: A snake the colour of jade teaches you to respect signs.

events.text: In Chengdu, an opera performer changes masks faster than the eye can follow. They say it is a sect technique.

effects.log: You see the flick of a wrist, once. It is enough to make your own hands faster.
He changes masks again. 'What trick?' he asks, with a new face.

events.text: The ground shakes in the night. Tiles fall, walls crack, and the whole town runs into the street in their sleeping clothes.

effects.log: You lift a beam off a family of four. The mother never lets you pay for anything again.

choices.text: Get the children to open ground

effects.log: You herd twenty children to the threshing floor and tell them stories until dawn.

events.text: Porters on the Tea Horse Road carry tea bricks twice their own weight over mountain passes into the west.

choices.text: Carry a load with them for a week

effects.log: Your legs will never be the same. Better, mostly. (15 taels)
They tell you about the passes, the snow and the monasteries beyond.

events.text: A Tang family courier asks you to carry a small sealed box to the next town. 'Do not open it. Truly.'

effects.log: The recipient gives you ten taels and a look of mild surprise that you are still alive.
'Wise,' says the courier. That is somehow more frightening.

events.text: Rafting down a Sichuan river on bamboo, the current speeds up. Ahead: rapids, and a very surprised heron.

ok.log: Spray, rocks, triumph. The heron flies off unimpressed.

fail.log: The raft breaks apart. You swim the last li.

effects.log: You walk the rest of the way, dry and smug. The raft reaches town before you.

events.text: A Chengdu restaurant offers free meals for a year to anyone who can finish its 'Nine Hells' chilli bowl.

ok.log: Nine hells, one hero. A year of free lunches.

fail.log: You make it to the fourth hell and retreat with honour.

effects.log: A monk finishes it without blinking. You never learn his name.

events.text: Golden monkeys on Mount Emei rob pilgrims of anything shiny. One has taken your purse.

ok.log: You get the purse back. The monkey keeps one coin as a fee.

fail.log: The monkey climbs higher than you ever will. Gone.

effects.log: You laugh. It is the best-dressed monkey on the mountain now.

events.text: An old physician in a Sichuan village treats bandits and constables alike, and nobody fights in her yard.

effects.log: You learn to set bones, sew wounds and keep your mouth shut. All three are useful.

choices.text: Ask her why she treats bandits

effects.log: 'Blood is red on everyone,' she says, and hands you a bucket.

events.text: A shrine on a Sichuan peak honours a swordsman who held the pass alone against an army. The offerings are all small knives.

effects.log: You leave your best knife. The wind sounds like applause.
The carvings list the army's numbers. They are impossible. You believe them anyway.

events.text: In thick mountain fog, you hear footsteps matching yours on the path behind.

ok.log: A would-be robber, who thinks better of it once he sees you.

fail.log: Three of them. You get away with a cut arm.

choices.text: Step off the path and wait

effects.log: A mule loaded with tea walks past, alone. You feel a little foolish.

events.text: A covered bridge in the Sichuan hills, full of travellers sheltering from the rain and sharing their food.

effects.log: Pickles, rice cakes and gossip from six villages. Nobody leaves hungry.
You wake with someone else's coat over you. Nobody claims it.

events.text: A Tang child, maybe eight, stops you from eating a mushroom by slapping it out of your hand. 'That one. Never.'

effects.log: The child looks very pleased and teaches you three more mushrooms to never eat.
'My aunt,' says the child. You decide not to ask about the aunt.
